impact_reviews.change: US-DC-04 disclose commercial relationships on every listing: commercial_disclosure on each of the eight tool listings (all NONE_KNOWN, declared 2026-10-09), fail-closed catalogue validation and the closed AISolutionsCatalog contract; domain API 1.28.0
impact_reviews.summary: New threat TH36: a commercial relationship with a listed provider is hidden or misstated. Each listing now carries a disclosure from a closed list (NONE_KNOWN with no type; DISCLOSED with at least one of referral fee, revenue share, reseller, sponsorship, ownership); both carry a statement and a declaration date. solutions_catalog() validates every listing with plain rules and the published JSON schema before returning; a missing or invalid disclosure (including DISCLOSED without a type or a statement) raises, GET ai-enablement/solutions answers 503 AI_SOLUTIONS_CATALOG_INVALID and nothing is served (the API keeps running; other AI enablement reads are unaffected). The listing builder never adds a disclosure by default. No relationship is invented: the eight listings are NONE_KNOWN, worded as 'is known' rather than 'does not exist', and the editorial statement says the declaration awaits advisor review; that review is not built (C-DISCLOSURE-EDITORIAL-REVIEW, gap recorded). AISolutionsCatalog changes from an open object with five required keys to the closed schema of the archived v2 solutions component; GET solutions keeps ai.enablement.read and the same reader roles (TH02 unchanged). access-policy.json changes only its version field (1.27.0 -> 1.28.0): no operation, capability, role or assurance row changed. The web client shows the label on every card, comparison column and archived listing as a named note.

impact_reviews.change: US-DC-04 archive edition nonprofit-ai-guidance-v2 with the v1 reader kept: migration 0043 widens the ai_content_snapshot edition check; guidance read and plan export contracts admit both editions
impact_reviews.summary: Migration 0043 drops and re-creates ai_content_snapshot_schema_version_check (the name PostgreSQL gave 0037's column check) as schema_version IN ('nonprofit-ai-guidance-v1','nonprofit-ai-guidance-v2'); re-creating it validates existing rows. No table, column, grant, role, RLS policy, trigger or function changes; snapshots and bindings stay insert-only, tenant-keyed and fenced (TH01); 0001-0042 are byte-identical. New saves capture v2; v1 rows are never relabelled or backfilled and are read by the retained v1 reader (ai_content_schema_v1.json is byte-identical, pinned by SHA-256 in a unit test) (TH32). The reader now requires the row label and the hashed payload label to agree and validates with that edition's reader, so a mislabelled, tampered or disclosure-stripped v2 archive answers 503 AI_GUIDANCE_UNREADABLE (TH36: an archived disclosure cannot be altered silently). The guidance read contract and the export document's guidance member become one closed variant per edition plus the unavailable variant, each binding its label to its payload shapes. The export package stays nonprofit-ai-plan-export-v1 with its frozen plan projection; exports issued before 0.39.0 replay unchanged, and new exports of v2-archived plans carry the disclosures inside their guidance (TH15: export authority, mediation and replay are unchanged). Residual: a consumer that validates exports against the earlier published document schema would reject v2 guidance.
